decisions.decision: The Foundation Repository's versioned Release Contract baseline lives in the machine-readable contract tree at contracts/release-contract/foundation.json (instance of contracts/schemas/release-contract.json) with a sibling contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json and a short contracts/release-contract/README.md. No copy is placed under docs/.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/documentation.md section 2 already declares contracts/release-contract/ as the machine-readable canonical location, and ci/components.json owns contracts/** with exactly one component (contracts), so ci-plan --tracked ownership stays single-owner. Keeping the instance out of docs/ keeps the Documentation policy 'one fact, one source of truth' intact.

decisions.decision: Resolve the release-contract.md seven-declaration requirement versus the narrow capability object by a two-document contract: contracts/schemas/release-contract.json is NOT modified (capability keeps id/name/status/evidence_ids), and the seven declarations plus the documentation.md section 5 references move into a new sibling schema contracts/schemas/capability-declaration-set.json, joined to the contract by capability id. contracts/release-contract/foundation.json references the declaration set through its verification entries; a Go test enforces a strict bijection of capability ids between the two files.
decisions.rationale: Extending release-contract.json is backward incompatible in three ways: (a) the seven items would have to be optional to keep contracts/fixtures/valid/release-contract.json valid, which means nothing forces the declaration and the release-contract.md requirement stays unmet; making them required breaks that fixture and every other Repository's contract, which the Secrets/Continuous-delivery policy expand->migrate->contract rule forbids in one step; (b) internal/contracts/contracts_test.go TestSchemasRejectSensitiveFieldNames fails on any schema file containing the substring 'credential', so 'credential scope' cannot be modelled inside contracts/schemas/release-contract.json under that name anyway; (c) internal/release.CompileContract hashes the contract bytes and rejects unknown fields, so widening the shared schema widens the promotion-gate blast radius. A separate set schema can make all seven items required with minItems/minLength while leaving the shared v1 contract untouched, and the bijection test removes the drift risk that motivates a single file.

decisions.decision: contracts/schemas/capability-declaration-set.json: additionalProperties false; required schema_version(const v1), id, kind(const capability-declaration-set), created_at(date-time), correlation_id, release(same semver pattern as release-contract.json), contract_ref, capabilities(minItems 1). Each capability requires id, name, user_action, observable_result, preview_exercise, external_dependencies{systems[],providers[],scopes[]}, outcome_conditions{success,failure,rollback}, evidence_retention{location,retention}, documentation{preview, optional stable}, owner_surfaces(minItems 1), evidence_schema, promotion_prerequisites(minItems 1); additionalProperties false at every level; optional exercise_ref.
decisions.rationale: The seven release-contract.md section 2 declarations map to user_action, observable_result, preview_exercise, external_dependencies, outcome_conditions, evidence_retention, documentation. documentation.md section 5 additionally requires a Stable anchor, a Preview anchor, a UI route, an exercise implementation reference, and an Evidence schema, which map to documentation.stable, documentation.preview, owner_surfaces, exercise_ref, evidence_schema. 'credential scope' is named 'scopes' because contracts/schemas is scanned for the substring 'credential'. documentation.stable and exercise_ref are optional at baseline because no Stable Release and no exercise implementation exist yet; requiring them would force fabricated references, which the V2-009 non-goals forbid. Only JSON Schema keywords supported by internal/contracts.Validate are used (const, enum, type, required, properties, additionalProperties:false, minItems, items, minLength, maxLength, pattern, format).

decisions.decision: The unexercised baseline is marked mechanically by release string '0.1.0-baseline', capability status 'preview' for every capability, and evidence_ids present but empty for every capability. Three invariants are asserted in Go: (B1) when the release prerelease identifier is 'baseline', every capability status must be 'preview' and every evidence_ids must be empty; (B2) status 'stable' requires non-empty evidence_ids, a documentation.stable anchor, and each evidence id resolving to an entry in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json; (B3) any evidence id listed by any capability must resolve in that index, so no invented id can ever appear.
decisions.rationale: The schema top level is additionalProperties:false, so a new boolean flag such as baseline:true is impossible without a breaking schema change. The release pattern ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[A-Za-z0-9.-]+)?$ already admits a prerelease identifier, so the marker needs zero schema change and is visible to internal/release.CompileContract, which surfaces the release string as CompiledContract.Version. B1 makes 'no Evidence yet' a machine-checked property instead of a comment; B2 and B3 are the anti-fabrication gate that keeps future promotions honest, and they hold vacuously for the baseline.

decisions.decision: Twelve mandatory user-facing capabilities, one per section of docs/product/user-facing-spec.md section 4, all at status preview with empty evidence_ids: cap-repository-registration (4.1), cap-requirement-intake (4.2), cap-backlog-visibility (4.3), cap-autonomous-resolution (4.4), cap-human-input-request (4.5), cap-preview-operation (4.6), cap-stable-promotion (4.7), cap-loop-control (4.8), cap-loop-self-update (4.9), cap-shared-resource-allocation (4.10), cap-provider-operation (4.11), cap-user-documentation (4.12). Stop variants (graceful/immediate/emergency), pause/resume/cancel, rollback and resume are declared as operations and outcome conditions inside their owning capability, not as separate capabilities.
decisions.rationale: docs/product/user-facing-spec.md section 4 is the canonical list of what the user can operate, and its twelve subsections are exactly journey-sized; section 8 items 1-13 are covered by that set. release-contract.md section 2 forbids substituting internal functions or test cases for the capability list, and docs/architecture/validation.md section 3 explicitly warns against decomposing capabilities down to API calls, so stop variants stay inside cap-loop-control. Every capability is preview because docs/stable/index.md records that no v2 Stable Release exists and docs/preview/index.md records that the v2 branch is not even a deployed Preview Release; assigning stable to anything would fabricate Evidence.

decisions.decision: Baseline verification lives in a new internal/contracts/release_contract_test.go function TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline, reached by make component-contracts (go test ./internal/contracts). It belongs to components 'contracts' (roots contracts/**) and 'internal-contracts' (roots internal/contracts/**), which both declare the same check target. It asserts: schema validity of both files against their schemas; capability id bijection and uniqueness in declared order; invariants B1/B2/B3; every documentation.preview and documentation.stable anchor exists exactly once as a literal in the referenced file; every evidence_schema path exists; every owner_surfaces entry is /owner/ or a path declared in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml; every verification entry starting with 'make ' names a target present in the Makefile; contract_ref equals the contract id and the two release strings are equal.
decisions.rationale: internal/contracts is the only package that already owns fixture-and-repository-invariant verification and already depends on component contracts, so no new component or dependency edge is introduced. Anchor and path checks implement docs/architecture/validation.md section 4 ('capability ごとに利用者文書への参照があることを Release Contract で検査する') and documentation.md section 5 ('文書 anchor がない capability、存在しない anchor はpromotion を止める'). Literal HTML anchors are used instead of heading slugs because the headings are Japanese and slug rules are not reproducible in a dependency-free test.

decisions.decision: internal/release.CompileContract is fixed to parse the canonical contract surface. Its decode struct gains id, kind, created_at, correlation_id, capability name/status/evidence_ids, verification and rollback{procedure,target}, so DisallowUnknownFields keeps rejecting drift while accepting a schema-valid contract; it additionally rejects any capability whose status is 'stable' with no evidence id. A new internal/release/contract_baseline_test.go compiles contracts/release-contract/foundation.json against docs/preview/capabilities.md bytes and asserts the twelve capability ids and Version 0.1.0-baseline, plus a negative case for an unknown field and for stable-without-evidence.
decisions.rationale: Measured on this worktree: CompileContract(contracts/fixtures/valid/release-contract.json, docs) returns 'release contract is incomplete'. The function that computes the ContractDigest consumed by PromotionGate therefore cannot read any schema-valid Release Contract, so a baseline that is never compilable by the gate would be decoration. The existing minimal-JSON test keeps passing because Go decoding leaves absent fields zero-valued, and the stable-without-evidence rejection duplicates invariant B2 inside the release component so the gate does not depend on the contracts test.

decisions.decision: ci/components.json adds "contracts/release-contract/**" to the release component's contract_dependencies. Nothing else in the manifest changes.
decisions.rationale: internal/release now reads the baseline instance, so the release component's evidence key must hash it; ci.evidenceKey only hashes roots, public_contracts and contract_dependencies, and without this entry a change to foundation.json would leave stale release evidence reusable, contradicting docs/architecture/validation.md section 11. Selection already fans out (contracts public_contracts is contracts/**), so this edit is about evidence-key honesty, not selection. The cost is a one-time full matrix because ci/** is in all_on_change.

decisions.decision: Documentation changes are pointer-and-anchor only: new docs/preview/capabilities.md holds one anchor plus a short Japanese heading per capability, each stating that the machine-readable declaration is canonical and that the capability is unexercised; docs/preview/index.md and docs/preview/stable-diff.md link to it and to contracts/release-contract/foundation.json; docs/stable/index.md gains one sentence that no v2 Stable capability exists and where the baseline lives. Full Preview operating instructions are NOT written now; they are recorded per capability in promotion_prerequisites.
decisions.rationale: The Documentation policy forbids hand-copying the same fact into several documents, so the prose of user_action and observable_result stays in the declaration set and the Preview document links to it. release-contract.md section 5 requires the Preview document to state what evidence is missing for promotion, which is exactly what the anchors carry at baseline. Writing complete Preview operating instructions for twelve capabilities that have never run in a Preview environment would describe unverified behaviour.

decisions.decision: foundation.json verification is the argv-level list that is executable today: 'devbox run --pure check', 'make component-contracts', 'make component-release', 'make ownership', 'go test ./internal/contracts -run TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline', 'go test ./internal/release -run TestCompileFoundationBaselineContract'. rollback.procedure is the git revert of the baseline commit followed by 'devbox run --pure check', and rollback.target is 'main-v1', the known recovery point recorded in docs/stable/index.md. Preview exercise commands are NOT put in verification; they live in each capability's preview_exercise and promotion_prerequisites.
decisions.rationale: verification is a string array with no place for future intent, so every entry must be runnable against this commit; docs/policies/README.md makes devbox run --pure check the common deterministic entrypoint. release-contract.md section 4 conditions 2-8 cannot be satisfied by any command in this repository today, so representing them as verification entries would be a false claim; representing them as per-capability promotion prerequisites keeps them auditable and keeps the promotion gate honest. rollback.target must be a real recovery point, and the only one that exists is the v1 loop on main.

risks: Widening the CompileContract decode struct could mask a real drift signal; mitigated by keeping DisallowUnknownFields and adding an explicit unknown-field negative test.
The two-file split can drift; mitigated by the strict capability-id bijection assertion and by contract_ref plus equal release strings.
Editing ci/components.json triggers all_on_change, so the whole matrix runs and every component evidence key rotates once. Expected, not a defect.

A new schema in contracts/schemas requires both fixtures; a missing or wrongly-shaped invalid fixture silently weakens TestSchemasAndFixtures, so the invalid fixture must fail under the internal/contracts validator subset (missing required field), not under an unsupported keyword such as uniqueItems.
Naming a field with the substring 'credential' in contracts/schemas fails TestSchemasRejectSensitiveFieldNames; the scopes field must carry scope names only and never values.

Declaring twelve capabilities makes every future Stable promotion exercise all twelve in Preview; that cost is intended by release-contract.md section 3 and must not be reduced by deleting capabilities from the baseline.

Escalate to product_orchestrator instead of improvising if the capability set must differ from docs/product/user-facing-spec.md section 4, if any capability needs status stable before a Preview exercise exists, or if contracts/schemas/release-contract.json must change after all.
